newsitem.title: USA: Calif. revenues $297 mln above forecast - report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. revenues $297 mln above forecast - report.

text.p: California general fund revenues for January were $297 million above the governor's 1997-1998 budget forecast of $4.947 billion, the state's Department of Finance said on Tuesday.
"Although this is encouraging, it is important to note that critical collection months lie ahead," the department said in its monthly revenue report.
The department said personal income tax receipts were $279 million more than the month's forecast, while withholding revenues were $5.0 million less than Gov. Pete Wilson's budget forecast.
Sales and use-tax revenues were $48 million more than the month's estimate while bank and corporation tax revenues were $15 million less than the month's forecast.

The Department of Finance said March would be the next significant month for the bank and corporation tax. The department said April would be critical for the personal income tax as well as the bank and corporation tax.
